horizontal-vertical-shapes.Rmd

Horizontal and Vertical Lines and Rectangles in R

How to add annotated horizontal and vertical lines in R.

Horizontal and Vertical Lines and Rectangles

Horizontal and vertical lines and rectangles that span an entire plot can be added via the shapes argument of update_layout() (or one at a time with add_shape()). Shapes added with these methods are added as layout shapes. These shapes are fixed to the endpoints of one axis, regardless of the range of the plot, and fixed to data coordinates on the other axis. The following shows some possibilities, try panning and zooming the resulting figure to see how the shapes stick to some axes:

library(plotly.core)
data("iris")

hline <- function(y = 0, color = "black") {
  go_shape(
    type = "line",
    x0 = 0,
    x1 = 1,
    xref = "paper",
    y0 = y,
    y1 = y,
    line = go_shape_line(color = color)
  )
}

iris |>
  go_figure() |>
  add_scatter(x = ~Petal.Length, y = ~Petal.Width, mode = "markers") |>
  update_layout(
    shapes = list(
      hline(0.9),
      go_shape(type = "rect", line = go_shape_line(color = "black"), x0 = 0.9, x1 = 2)
    ),
    plot_bgcolor = "#e5ecf6"
  )

The shapes can also be filled with a specified color using fillcolor and the lines can also be changed to dotted lines using the dash parameter.

library(plotly.core)
data("iris")

vline <- function(x = 0, color = "green") {
  go_shape(
    type = "line",
    y0 = 0,
    y1 = 1,
    yref = "paper",
    x0 = x,
    x1 = x,
    line = go_shape_line(color = color, dash = "dot")
  )
}

iris |>
  go_figure() |>
  add_scatter(x = ~Petal.Length, y = ~Petal.Width, mode = "markers") |>
  update_layout(
    plot_bgcolor = "#e5ecf6",
    shapes = list(
      vline(2.5),
      go_shape(
        type = "rect",
        fillcolor = "red",
        line = go_shape_line(color = "red"),
        opacity = 0.2,
        y0 = 0.9,
        y1 = 2.6,
        x0 = 0.5,
        x1 = 7.5
      )
    )
  )

Adding Text Annotations

Text annotations can optionally be added next to a shape with a text-only scatter trace (add_scatter(mode = "text")), positioned using the x and y arguments. The stock prices below are weekly closing prices of six tech stocks, normalized to their value on January 1, 2018:

library(plotly.core)

stocks_url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plotly/plotly.py/main/plotly/package_data/datasets/stocks.csv.gz"
stocks_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".csv.gz")
download.file(stocks_url, stocks_file, quiet = TRUE)
stock <- read.csv(stocks_file)
names(stock) <- c("Dates", "GOOG", "AAPL", "AMZN", "META", "NFLX", "MSFT")
tickers <- c("GOOG", "AAPL", "AMZN", "META", "NFLX", "MSFT")

hline <- function(y = 0, color = "black") {
  go_shape(
    type = "line",
    x0 = 0,
    x1 = 1,
    xref = "paper",
    y0 = y,
    y1 = y,
    line = go_shape_line(color = color, dash = "dot")
  )
}

decline <- go_shape(
  type = "rect",
  fillcolor = "green",
  line = go_shape_line(color = "green"),
  opacity = 0.2,
  y0 = 0.6,
  y1 = 2.25,
  x0 = "2018-10-01",
  x1 = "2018-12-17"
)

fig <- go_figure()
for (tk in tickers) {
  fig <- fig |>
    add_scatter(x = stock$Dates, y = stock[[tk]], name = tk, mode = "lines")
}

fig <- fig |>
  add_scatter(
    showlegend = FALSE,
    mode = "text",
    x = c("2018-11-01", "2019-09-20"),
    y = c(2.2, 0.95),
    text = c("decline", "Jan 1, 2018 baseline")
  ) |>
  update_layout(
    legend = go_legend(title = go_legend_title(text = "company")),
    shapes = list(decline, hline(1)),
    xaxis = go_xaxis(title = "date"),
    yaxis = go_yaxis(title = "value"),
    plot_bgcolor = "#e5ecf6"
  )

fig

Extra formatting of the annotation can be done by adding textfont argument.

library(plotly.core)

stocks_url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plotly/plotly.py/main/plotly/package_data/datasets/stocks.csv.gz"
stocks_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".csv.gz")
download.file(stocks_url, stocks_file, quiet = TRUE)
stock <- read.csv(stocks_file)
names(stock) <- c("Dates", "GOOG", "AAPL", "AMZN", "META", "NFLX", "MSFT")
tickers <- c("GOOG", "AAPL", "AMZN", "META", "NFLX", "MSFT")

hline <- function(y = 0, color = "black") {
  go_shape(
    type = "line",
    x0 = 0,
    x1 = 1,
    xref = "paper",
    y0 = y,
    y1 = y,
    line = go_shape_line(color = color, dash = "dot")
  )
}

decline <- go_shape(
  type = "rect",
  fillcolor = "green",
  line = go_shape_line(color = "green"),
  opacity = 0.2,
  y0 = 0.6,
  y1 = 2.25,
  x0 = "2018-10-01",
  x1 = "2018-12-17"
)

fig <- go_figure()
for (tk in tickers) {
  fig <- fig |>
    add_scatter(x = stock$Dates, y = stock[[tk]], name = tk, mode = "lines")
}

fig <- fig |>
  add_scatter(
    showlegend = FALSE,
    mode = "text",
    x = c("2018-11-10", "2019-08-20"),
    y = c(2.2, 0.95),
    text = c("decline", "Jan 1, 2018 baseline"),
    textfont = go_font(
      color = c("#000000", "blue"),
      size = c(20, 20),
      family = c("Open Sans", "Times New Roman")
    )
  ) |>
  update_layout(
    legend = go_legend(title = go_legend_title(text = "company")),
    plot_bgcolor = "#e5ecf6",
    shapes = list(decline, hline(1)),
    xaxis = go_xaxis(title = "date"),
    yaxis = go_yaxis(title = "value")
  )

Adding to Multiple Facets / Subplots

The same line or box can be added to several subplots of a make_subplots() figure by passing row and col to add_shape(). Using "x domain" as the xref makes the line span the whole width of that subplot.

library(plotly.core)

stocks_url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plotly/plotly.py/main/plotly/package_data/datasets/stocks.csv.gz"
stocks_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".csv.gz")
download.file(stocks_url, stocks_file, quiet = TRUE)
stock <- read.csv(stocks_file)
names(stock) <- c("Dates", "GOOG", "AAPL", "AMZN", "META", "NFLX", "MSFT")
tickers <- c("GOOG", "AAPL", "AMZN", "META", "NFLX", "MSFT")

# which subplots get the baseline and the "decline" rectangle
has_hline <- c(GOOG = TRUE, AAPL = TRUE, AMZN = FALSE, META = FALSE, NFLX = FALSE, MSFT = FALSE)
has_rect <- c(GOOG = TRUE, AAPL = FALSE, AMZN = TRUE, META = FALSE, NFLX = TRUE, MSFT = FALSE)

fig <- make_subplots(
  rows = 3,
  cols = 2,
  subplot_titles = paste0("company=", tickers)
)

for (i in seq_along(tickers)) {
  tk <- tickers[[i]]
  row <- (i - 1) %/% 2 + 1
  col <- (i - 1) %% 2 + 1
  fig <- fig |>
    add_scatter(x = stock$Dates, y = stock[[tk]], name = tk, mode = "lines", row = row, col = col)
  if (has_rect[[tk]]) {
    fig <- fig |>
      add_shape(
        type = "rect",
        fillcolor = "green",
        line = go_shape_line(color = "green"),
        opacity = 0.2,
        y0 = 0.6,
        y1 = 2,
        x0 = "2018-10-01",
        x1 = "2018-12-17",
        row = row,
        col = col
      ) |>
      add_scatter(
        showlegend = FALSE,
        mode = "text",
        x = "2018-11-05",
        y = 1.9,
        text = "decline",
        row = row,
        col = col
      )
  }
  if (has_hline[[tk]]) {
    fig <- fig |>
      add_shape(
        type = "line",
        x0 = 0,
        x1 = 1,
        xref = "x domain",
        y0 = 1,
        y1 = 1,
        line = go_shape_line(color = "black", dash = "dot"),
        row = row,
        col = col
      ) |>
      add_scatter(
        showlegend = FALSE,
        mode = "text",
        x = "2019-10-20",
        y = 0.95,
        text = "Jan 1, 2018 baseline",
        row = row,
        col = col
      )
  }
}

fig <- fig |>
  update_xaxes(title = "", zeroline = FALSE, showline = FALSE, showticklabels = FALSE) |>
  update_xaxes(title = "Date", showticklabels = TRUE, row = 3) |>
  update_yaxes(range = c(0.5, 2)) |>
  update_yaxes(title = "value", col = 1) |>
  update_yaxes(title = "", showticklabels = FALSE, col = 2) |>
  update_annotations(font = go_font(size = 10)) |>
  update_layout(
    legend = go_legend(title = go_legend_title(text = "company")),
    plot_bgcolor = "#e5ecf6"
  )

fig
